A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SMART by the same author team. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across substantial rewriting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original calibration experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, and supplementary accuracy, calibration, and corruption analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds baseline comparisons, objective-training analyses, adversarial boundary-distance measurements, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: v2 replaces SoftECE with a shifted Charbonnier-smoothed bin-mean objective. The 49-parameter temperature network remains, but its temperature floor changes from 1e-6 to 0.1, and Algorithm 1 omits v1's explicit gap-standardization step. These revise the reported optimization and input-processing procedure.

E1.justification: The CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet, ImageNet-C, ImageNet-LT, and ImageNet-Sketch coverage is retained. v2 Figure 1a adds a limited adversarial test scenario: C&W perturbations on CIFAR-10 to assess the relationship between margin and decision-boundary distance.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Group Calibration, ProCal, and Feature Clipping to the existing post-hoc comparators. Table 3 adds UWG, DFL, and MDCA comparisons. The validation-size comparison also replaces Spline with Group Calibration and includes Vanilla.

E3.justification: The reported ImageNet-family calibration split changes from 50 samples in v1 Section 4.1 to 20% of the official validation set in v2 Appendix J. The validation-size study changes from ResNet-50 on ImageNet and ImageNet-C to ImageNet ViT-B/32 with 2–512 samples. These are substantive reported protocol revisions; the PDFs do not establish that all retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds NLL/ECE training trajectories, SoftECE versus Charbonnier loss and gradient comparisons, attack–margin analysis, bandwidth/smoothing sensitivity tables, and learned margin–temperature case studies. It extends the loss ablation while removing v1's bin-count sensitivity and scalar-versus-vector fitting curves. Earlier corruption and margin-group analyses largely persist.

E5.justification: Five-seed evaluations and ten-run timing remain. Main ECE uncertainties largely move to v2 Table 7, but Vanilla dispersion and Table 4's loss-ablation uncertainties disappear. Appendix G replaces v1's best-of-five captions with references to the main five-seed protocol while retaining the numerical entries. These change reporting without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: Numerous entries are added or revised. SMART's ImageNet ViT-B/16 ECE changes from 0.86% to 0.48% in Table 1, and new comparator, Charbonnier-ablation, and sensitivity results appear. PTS runtime changes from 90.44 seconds in v1 Table 3 to 1050.44 seconds in v2 Table 6. Revised methods and splits prevent interpreting cross-version ECE changes as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A.1 corrects v1's reversed temperature-bound endpoints and distinguishes target-confidence regimes. Sections 3.1–3.4 and Appendices A.2–A.4 add smCE, a Charbonnier upper-bound theorem, kernel and bin-aggregation bounds, a within-bin homogeneity assumption, and directional-derivative arguments about NLL/calibration mismatch.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes lightweight gap-based recalibration and SoftECE's bias–variance/data-efficiency benefits. v2 makes formal NLL/calibration mismatch and smCE control through Charbonnier-SoftECE central contributions. The lightweight margin-based approach and broad state-of-the-art calibration claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes calibration metrics from proper scoring rules and acknowledges that the top-two margin is not universally sufficient, particularly when ambiguity involves many non-top classes. Appendix K introduces architecture-dependent, non-monotonic temperature mappings. Section 4.4 shifts the interpretation from exceptional data scarcity performance toward improvement as validation data increases.

D1.justification: v2 documents Adam with learning rate 0.005, the complete bin-mean loss, 15 soft bins, bandwidth 0.05, smoothing parameter 0.001, minibatch pseudocode, and crop/flip augmentation. The advertised code location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. v1's explicit weight-decay value is no longer supplied.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially around adaptive recalibration, calibration objectives, and evaluation metrics. Additions include smooth-calibration/proper-loss theory, AdaTS, local temperature scaling, Feature Clipping, UWG, and MDCA. SMART is repositioned around a direct hardness indicator and calibration-centric optimization, with more explicit differentiation from prior SoftECE approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and methodology are extensively rewritten. Margin theory now precedes separate NLL-mismatch, Charbonnier-objective, and SMART-framework sections. Runtime and margin-perspective discussions are reorganized into appendices. The title adds 'Scaling', and 'logit gap' largely becomes 'margin'.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. The opening overview figure is replaced, Figure 2 is partly redesigned, and new diagnostic plots and sensitivity tables appear. Table 1 gains comparator columns and a separate appendix uncertainty table; retained appendix figures are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects v1's reversed temperature bounds, broadens comparisons, improves implementation documentation, and states useful limitations. However, new central theory has unresolved defects: Proposition A.7 uses an overconfidence lower bound as an upper bound in its NLL argument, and an increasing calibration witness alone does not establish increasing smCE. Appendix J.2 also claims less than 0.2-point sensitivity despite Table 14 containing 0.66 and 3.11 in the same row. These gains and new validity/reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
